adopted.note: PASS 4 (2026-07-29) removed exceeds_200k_tokens entirely: it rendered as a bare "+" on the window size ("of 1M+"), unreadable without knowing the rule, and it signals long-context premium PRICING -- the same reason cost.total_cost_usd is omitted (DISABLE_COST_WARNINGS=1). Also stripped the "(1M context)" suffix from model.display_name so the window is stated once, not twice; renamed the pacing marker from "fast" (which collided with the fast_mode segment) to an explicit multiple, "2.2x pace"; switched burn_rate to tenths-of-a-percent precision because whole percent reported 4.5x for a true 5.4x; and made the context bar 5 cells of thin rules (━/─) instead of 8 of block shading, with rounded rather than floored cell counts so 18% is not a visually empty bar. PASS 3 (2026-07-29) added rate_limits.*.resets_at, a burn-rate pacing signal, an 8-cell context bar, ANSI threshold colours, and statusLine.refreshInterval=60. Pace = used% vs elapsed% of the window; green <=125, yellow <=175, red above, suppressed under 15% used, with absolute overrides at 75/90. A 'fast' word appears only past the warn band. Renders in ~50ms. PASS 2 note follows -- second pass after auditing all ~40 documented payload fields against the 12 in use. fast_mode matters because Opus 5 fast mode is $10/$50 per Mtok and the state drifts (2.1.219 fixed stale fast-mode on Remote Control). context_window_size disambiguates ctx% -- a fallbackModel hop to Haiku silently drops 1M to 200k, previously invisible. exceeds_200k_tokens folded into the size as a trailing '+' (long-context premium marker) instead of its own segment. fires when a turn ends on an API error; matchers are error types (rate_limit, overloaded, authentication_failed, oauth_org_not_allowed, billing_error, invalid_request, model_not_found, server_error, max_output_tokens, unknown). Wired with matcher "" to catch all. Closes a gap for the unattended posture (CLAUDE_CODE_RETRY_WATCHDOG=1, headless mac mini): the docs do not state that Stop also fires on the error path, so a session dying on rate_limit would otherwise be silent. StopFailure discards output and exit code EXCEPT terminalSequence, so the hook emits an OSC 777 escape (ESC ]777;notify;<title>;<body> BEL) which ghostty renders as a desktop notification (desktop-notifications defaults to true). The payload field carrying the error type is undocumented, so the script scans the payload for any string matching the known enum rather than guessing a key. 9-case regression test in hooks/stop-failure-notify.test.sh

adopted.feature: move `make validate` from per-edit hook to commit time
adopted.note: DELETED ~/.claude/.claude/settings.json, whose project-scope PostToolUse hook (matcher Write|Edit|MultiEdit) ran `make -C ~/.claude pre-commit` on EVERY file edit. That target is `@$(MAKE) validate`, i.e. the whole suite -- formatting, ruff, ty, stylua, luacheck, hook tests -- over the whole repo, per edit. The matcher also named MultiEdit, a tool that no longer exists. Root cause of the hook: jj has no hook system and does not run git's hooks even in a colocated repo, so .git/hooks/pre-commit never fires on `jj describe`/`jj commit`, and the per-edit hook was compensating. Fixed at the right layer instead: skills/committing-changes step 3 now states validation is mandatory on the jj path and names `make validate` as this repo's gate. Also recorded there that `jj fix` is NOT a substitute -- it pipes file content through a tool and keeps what comes back, so it carries formatters (ruff format, stylua) but never report-only checks (ruff check, ty, luacheck, hook tests)

Underlines misspelled words in the prompt input as you type. Two-part change: aspell was added to packages/brew.txt and installed (0.60.8.2), because no checker was on PATH and the binary logs "[spellcheck] no checker found on PATH (looked for aspell, hunspell, ispell); spell checking stays off" and silently does nothing. USER SETTINGS ONLY -- the binary explicitly rejects project/local blocks: "a spellcheck block in project or local settings is ignored, whatever else is configured; set it in your user settings (~/.claude/settings.json) instead". Full schema is {enabled, checker, language, color}, all optional, enabled defaults false; left at bare enabled:true so the checker auto-resolves to aspell and the color falls back to the theme error color || 2026-08-20 follow-up, checker choice and tuning. CHECKER: kept aspell, and the reason is NOT the usual one. Traced the 2.1.238 pipe protocol: it classifies misspelled/correct/unrecognized and DISCARDS the ispell suggestion list, so aspells historically better suggestions are worth nothing here -- the choice turns on dictionary availability, and that is decisive. Homebrews aspell bundles 739 dictionary files including en_US (326MB in Cellar); Homebrews hunspell 1.7.3 depends only on readline+gettext and ships NO dictionaries, so it needs .aff/.dic files placed in ~/Library/Spelling by hand and otherwise starts, finds nothing, and the binary logs "a missing dictionary usually means spellcheck.language needs setting". aspell is also first in the binarys auto-detect order [aspell, hunspell, ispell], so checker:auto resolves to it with no setting. ispell is not a real candidate. Revisit only for non-English or heavy compound-word text, where hunspells morphology genuinely wins. || APT: needs BOTH aspell and aspell-en. The Debian aspell package ships no dictionary, so aspell alone installs a checker that can never start. Homebrew does not have this split. || CONFIG: nothing more to set in settings.json -- the full schema is only {enabled, checker, language, color}, and checker/language/color all resolve correctly by default (auto -> aspell, en_US, theme error color). The config that actually matters is aspells own, added as a new stow package dotfiles/aspell: .aspell.conf plus a 119-word .aspell.en_US.pws. MEASURED NEED: piping CLAUDE.md + rules/ + skills/ through aspell flagged jj 133 times, plus revset, oplog, evolog, fileset, frontmatter, dotfiles, typecheck, glhf, uv, jq, gh -- on two lines of ordinary text it produced 6 false positives against 3 real typos, which is worse than useless for a live underline. With the word list the same sample flags only genuine typos. || THREE GOTCHAS, all silent-failure: (1) the .pws header lang must be `en`, NOT `en_US` -- personal_ws-1.1 en_US parses without complaint and loads zero words. (2) `personal` must be set EXPLICITLY in .aspell.conf even though the value is byte-identical to what `aspell config personal` reports as the default; left unset the dictionary never loads. (3) aspell expands neither ~ nor $HOME in that path -- both forms parse and then silently fail -- so it must stay relative, which is also what keeps it portable to Linux. Regression check, from any cwd: echo "jj mmap teh" | aspell -a | grep ^& should flag teh only. || run-together is deliberately OFF. It masked gotcha 2 during setup (revset passes as rev+set whether or not the dictionary loaded) and it swallows dropped-space typos, the most common kind: thebug parses as the+bug. Verified thebug/seperate/isue are all caught with it off. || 2026-08-20 pass 3, color + commit gate + typo sweep. COLOR: set to #eba0ac, Catppuccin Mocha Maroon. Picking Red would have been a NO-OP -- the theme override error is #f38ba8, which is exactly what spellcheck already falls back to. Maroon is the only Mocha accent not bound to a semantic role in themes/catppuccin-mocha.json, so it cannot collide: warning is #f9e2af, merged/autoAccept #cba6f7, claude/fastMode #fab387. TENSION (SINCE RESOLVED -- Teej reversed the hex decline the same day and hooks/status.sh is now truecolor too) with the then-standing truecolor-hex decline (statusLine, 2026-07-29, which preferred ANSI names so colors survive a theme switch): that tradeoff is real here too -- a hex maroon will NOT follow a theme change, whereas omitting color would. It is accepted deliberately, because ANSI has no maroon and ansi:red resolves to the terminals red, i.e. back to the no-op. Revert to no color key to restore theme-following behavior. || COMMIT GATE: added codespell v2.4.3 to .pre-commit-config.yaml, so it also runs in make validate and CI. Chose codespell over an aspell hook on purpose -- aspell answers is-this-in-a-dictionary, which on 157 tracked files full of identifiers means permanent false positives and an unusable gate, while codespell only flags KNOWN misspellings. The two are complementary, not redundant: aspell underlines the prompt live and tolerates noise; codespell gates what lands and must stay silent. Verified non-vacuous -- a planted "sentance"/"recieving" file fails the hook. || Three codespell false positives are suppressed, all confirmed by hand: --ignore-regex on the literal [Cc]ontext, because the jq regex in hooks/status.sh tokenizes to "ontext"; and an exclude for dotfiles/lscolors/.local/share/lscolors.sh (generated LS_COLORS globs where *.caf and *.sav are file extensions) and for this baseline.json (its regression command deliberately contains teh/seperate/isue). || TYPO SWEEP: codespell over all 157 tracked files found ZERO real misspellings -- every hit was one of the three false positives above. history.jsonl and the runtime dirs are gitignored so pre-commit never sees them, and they must never be auto-corrected regardless: history.jsonl is a verbatim record of what Teej typed. A second aspell pass over prose added this session surfaced only vocabulary gaps, no errors, and grew the personal dictionary from 119 to 173 words (tooling names, jj/git vocabulary, OpenSSL/LibreSSL/LuaRocks-style mixed-case terms, which need exact-case entries because a lowercase .pws entry does not match internal capitals).

adopted.feature: voice.enabled (migrated off the voiceEnabled legacy alias)
adopted.introducedVersion: pre-2.1.238 (surfaced by a 2.1.239 bullet, not introduced by it)
adopted.note: Replaces "voiceEnabled": true with the nested object. NOT a new-in-window feature -- voice?.enabled is already present in the 2.1.238 binary, so this is pre-baseline drift that the 2.1.239 bullet ("voice dictation was enabled via the voice.enabled setting") merely exposed. Verified in the 2.1.241 binary: resolution is qdo(e) => (e.voice?.enabled ?? e.voiceEnabled) === true, so nested wins and the flat key was a working fallback, not broken. Schemastore calls voiceEnabled a "Legacy alias for voice.enabled; prefer the voice object", and the docs say the voice object is what /voice writes automatically -- so migrating aligns the file with what the product itself would write. Unlike additionalMarketplaces/extraKnownMarketplaces there is NO both-at-once rejection here, but only one spelling is kept. GAIN: unlocks the two sibling keys the flat alias cannot express -- mode ("hold" default | "tap" = tap to start, tap to stop+submit) and autoSubmit (submit on key release in hold mode, transcript >= 3 words). Both deliberately left unset at their defaults, per the standing rule in this ledger against writing keys whose value equals the default (see includeGitInstructions, dialogExpiry). ODDITY worth remembering: the feature-gate shape in the binary (Q9o.voice.shape()) still registers ONLY voiceEnabled, while the main settings schema carries the nested voice object -- which is why both spellings remain accepted. Also note the schemastore description links to settings#available-settings, an anchor that no longer exists: the key reference moved to its own page, docs/en/settings-reference.

adopted.feature: custom theme brought to full palette parity (4 missing keys, 1 dead key, 1 mis-mapped accent)
adopted.introducedVersion: pre-baseline -- keys accrued across releases before 2.1.241; NO release note ever named them
adopted.note: Found by the new step 6 (schema-completeness), NOT by the release-notes pass -- the file had been rotting since 2026-04-23 and no changelog bullet in any window would have surfaced it. Theme loader validates SILENTLY: `if (Object.hasOwn(basePalette,k) && isValidColor(v)) merged[k]=v` -- unknown keys are dropped with no warning, no error, no --debug line, and absent keys fall back to the built-in base. messageActionsBackground had 0 occurrences in the 2.1.246 binary and had been inert for four months; replaced by composerSidebarBackground, which is live for this config specifically because tui is "fullscreen". THE REAL DEFECT was `background`: it reads like a surface fill but is an ACCENT FOREGROUND (cyan in every built-in). Set to #313244 (Surface0) it rendered at 1.3:1 against Base #1e1e2e -- effectively invisible text -- vs 8.2:1 for the built-in it replaced; now #89dceb (Sky) at 10.5:1, kept distinct from planMode #94e2d5 (Teal). Accent-vs-surface is decidable without assuming a terminal background: surfaces INVERT between the light and dark built-ins (userMessageBackground 240->55), accents keep hue and BRIGHTEN (background 153->204). composerSidebarBackground calibrated from the built-in ratio 38/55 = 0.69 x #313244 -> #222230, nearest real catppuccin swatch is Base #1e1e2e. skill/effortUltra/autoAccept are the same value in all six built-ins, hence all mauve. Two 2.1.246 fixes also make this file more accurate for free: custom diffAdded/diffRemoved and dimmed variants were being IGNORED until now, and promptBorder no longer gets clobbered to cyan by /rename.

adopted.feature: hook stdout JSON emitted via jq instead of hand-rolled sed escaping
adopted.reason: 2.1.248: 'Fixed hooks silently treating a stdout {…} object that isn't valid JSON as plain text; it's now reported as a hook error with the parse message.' session-title.sh and user-prompt-submit/project-context.sh both escaped with sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g' -- backslash and quote only, NOT control characters. A cwd containing a tab or newline (legal on APFS) emitted a raw U+0009 inside a JSON string, which RFC 8259 forbids; reproduced and confirmed rejected by jq's parser. Before 2.1.248 that silently dropped the per-prompt context or the session title; after it, the same input surfaces a hook error on every prompt. Replaced both emit sites with jq -cn --arg, which escapes control chars correctly. jq was already a hard dependency of session-title.sh (lines 13/16) and stop-failure-notify.sh, so no new dependency. Verified: valid JSON for a tab-containing cwd and for the normal repo cwd, and the existing-title early-exit path still emits nothing.

DECLINED 2026-08-28 after measuring, and the measurement reversed the recommendation. 2.1.251: 'Added a per-session prompt-cache line to /cost ... and a matching prompt_cache object for status line scripts.' Confirmed shape at the assembly site (function sqe): {warm, caching_observed, ttl, expires_at, requests, misses, expected_rebuilds, hit_ratio, cache_write_tokens, miss_recache_tokens, last_miss_at, recache_tokens_if_cold}; the whole object is omitted while requests===0. Captured 15 real samples by temporarily teeing status.sh stdin (tee since removed; status.sh restored byte-identical). THE COUNTDOWN IS USELESS: expires_at is a ROLLING 1h refreshed on every request, not a fixed deadline -- ttl_left never left 3545-3574s (59.1-59.6 min) across every sample in two concurrent sessions. It only decays while idle, i.e. when nobody is reading the statusline. That killed both shapes originally proposed. hit_ratio also measured as session-age rather than health: 79%->87% on a young session, pinned 95% here, drifting up monotonically as the shared prefix amortizes. The only actionable fields are misses / expected_rebuilds / caching_observed (all 0/0/true throughout = the healthy default), which would fit quota_seg's 'healthy stays bare' precedent. Teej chose to leave status.sh alone. REVISIT with this shape if ever wanted: absent when misses==0 && expected_rebuilds==0 && caching_observed; 'cache N miss <miss_recache_tokens>' red on a real miss; 'cache N rebuilds' yellow; 'cache off' red when caching_observed is false. Also measured: recache_tokens_if_cold scales with context (202k at 20% ctx vs 56k at 6%), so it is the right number to pair WITH a miss, not to display standing.
